l0.headline: Oasis at Heaton Park: a Britpop-and-Madchester singalong day, building from warm walk-in to a sold-out Manchester homecoming

picks.name: The Stone Roses
picks.why: Madchester royalty that sets the local, nostalgic tone as gates open.
picks.action: Open the walk-in playlist with 'Waterfall' at moderate volume while queues are longest.

picks.name: The Verve
picks.why: Ashcroft's own band bridges the walk-in to tonight's support act.
picks.action: Place 'Bitter Sweet Symphony' mid-playlist and cue the screens to show the gate-to-stage map.

picks.name: Blur
picks.why: Britpop rivals-turned-peers give the crowd a friendly debate and a singalong.
picks.action: Run 'Parklife' and 'Girls & Boys' around 17:00 to lift the energy as the field fills.

picks.name: Pulp
picks.why: Mid-90s anthems cater to the core 35-55 Britpop audience.
picks.action: Schedule 'Common People' as a crowd-sing moment and have the PA hosts encourage early entry.

picks.name: The Charlatans
picks.why: Northern indie staple that fits the Manchester-area crowd.
picks.action: Use 'The Only One I Know' as a transition to higher tempo tracks.

picks.name: Cast
picks.why: Stretch: tonight's support act; playing their hits right before they go on primes the crowd.
picks.action: Close the playlist with 'Walkaway' and 'Alright' in the final 10 minutes before the first act.

picks.name: Cast
picks.why: Scouse Britpop veterans with a loyal following and hits that already match the crowd.
picks.action: Confirm the 17:30 start with stage management and prep a quick changeover crew for 18:15.

picks.name: The Lathums
picks.why: Rising indie-guitar act from Wigan with a Britpop-inspired sound and a strong northern fanbase.
picks.action: Flag them to the venue's local-talent team and offer a pre-show acoustic spot at the entrance stage.

picks.name: Sam Fender
picks.why: Stretch: a big-name Northern songwriter whose anthemic rock appeals to the same generation of fans.
picks.action: Add to the sponsor-friendly 'next-gen guitar' playlist and in-venue screen content during changeover.

picks.name: Local craft lager and cask ale bar
picks.why: Pints are the default for a Britpop-nostalgic, mostly adult crowd.
picks.action: Add extra beer tap stations at the main bars and put a 2-pint fast lane near the entrance.

picks.name: Pie and mash stand
picks.why: Comfort food on a long standing day fits Northern tastes.
picks.action: Position the stand near the walk-in queue and offer a pie-and-pint combo.

picks.name: Chippy-style fish and chips kiosk
picks.why: Classic British festival food everyone recognises.
picks.action: Set up two serving lines and a bin-heavy zone to keep the field clean.

picks.name: Curry Mile-inspired street food truck
picks.why: Stretch: Manchester's Rusholme curry scene is a local favourite and offers a flavourful alternative.
picks.action: Invite a Rusholme vendor to run a pop-up with a handheld curry wrap and vegetarian options.

picks.name: Fred Perry
picks.why: Classic British heritage label that matches the Britpop and terrace-style fanbase; sponsor-fit 9/10.
picks.action: Host a small pop-up merch stand near the gates with limited-edition tour-day polos.

picks.name: Adidas Originals
picks.why: Long tied to Oasis and Manchester casual culture; sponsor-fit 9/10.
picks.action: Set up a trainer-customisation station and a queue-managed photo wall.

picks.name: Stone Island
picks.why: Terrace-fashion staple among the core crowd; sponsor-fit 7/10.
picks.action: Offer a small display and a clear branding area, with security aware of high-value items.

picks.name: Carlsberg
picks.why: Stretch: a mainstream lager brand with broad reach among a beer-drinking crowd; sponsor-fit 7/10.
picks.action: Install branded bar signage and a refill-cup scheme to reduce waste.

picks.name: Northern Quarter bars
picks.why: Indie-music-centred bars and venues fit the crowd's taste for guitar music.
picks.action: Publish a map with a Northern Quarter bar crawl and tram timings.

picks.name: Night & Day Cafe
picks.why: Iconic Manchester live music venue with a strong indie reputation.
picks.action: Share the venue's late-night schedule in the exit communications.

picks.action: Lead the 15:00 gate-open block with 2-3 upbeat Drake tracks, radio edits only.

picks.why: An LA hometown anthem-maker whose hits unite both crowds.
picks.action: Cue 'Alright' and 'HUMBLE.' (clean edits) as the mid-block energy peak around 15:30.

picks.why: Toronto-born with massive LA stadium credibility, so he's a shared favorite.
picks.action: Slot 'Blinding Lights' and 'Can't Feel My Face' at 15:45 to build momentum.

picks.why: Quintessential LA rock that Canadian fans also sing along to.
picks.action: Play 'Californication' and 'Can't Stop' as a 16:00 singalong pair.

picks.action: Place 'Sorry' or 'Peaches' in the 16:05 pocket and cue the video board.
